Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J38/J38nB427.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Zhulangsheng of Qingcheng. Zhulang Chesheng first describes the world as a jewel and a jeweled net, with Buddhas, ancestors and beings appearing without obstruction, and explicitly quotes scripture. He then gives his staff a voice that accuses the old monk of sounding like a lecturer on the Perfection of Wisdom scripture. Striking and drawing with it, he smashes the jewel and tears the net: sun and moon may shine, seas surge, things grow and decline, and teachers and beings proceed according to their times. The quotation supports the opening vision, but the staff's enacted critique prevents clinging to its conceptual framework as another thing that must be preserved.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Monk Tianyin: In a letter to the layman Cao Nianzi, Tianyin Yuanxiu responds to repeated reports of suffering. He says that rich and poor alike are caught in trouble, then quotes the Buddha's complete Diamond Sutra verse about conditioned things as dreams, illusions, bubbles, shadows, dew, and lightning. Tianyin applies the quotation to body and mind, rank, wealth, and affliction: seeing their lack of fixed reality lets one act amid ordinary demands without being mastered by them. The verse is the Buddha's inherited speech; the explanation and advice to Cao are Tianyin's own.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Poshan: In Poshan Haiming's hall sermon, a monk first asks about the true character of things and receives a blow. Poshan then tells the assembly that he had dreamed of lay visitors Yin and Dai asking him to preach. He calls family, property, official rank, awakening, and even release dreams before quoting the complete Buddha verse. Poshan immediately asks what an open-eyed dream is, leaving the assembly without an answer. When Yin later kneels and asks him to explain, Poshan strikes him and withdraws. The citation starts the live test; the blow is Poshan's response, not part of the Buddha's verse.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Expanded Record of Chan Master Cishou Huaishen: In Cishou Huaishen's hall sermon, the Buddha's complete verse is recited first: conditioned things are to be seen as dreams, illusions, bubbles, and shadows. Cishou then turns the instruction into his own question: if that is how conditioned things are viewed, how should the unconditioned be viewed? His answer invokes an obstruction in the eye that even a skilled physician cannot pick out. The pair in the headword belongs to the earlier quoted verse; Cishou is the later questioner and commentator, and the eye image is his local challenge to treating the scriptural formula as a finished answer.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Fangrongxi: In a short instruction, Fangrong Ruxi asks what the 'king of the teaching who breaks existence' actually reveals. He tries several familiar doctrinal verses as possible answers, including the complete Diamond Sutra verse with these dream, illusion, bubble, and shadow images. Each is framed as 'Could it be this?' Fangrong says that merely answering in that way would let talkative teachers borrow the title without showing their own understanding. He closes by saying the wooden elder, his staff, will have to test anyone claiming more. The verse is inherited Buddha speech raised as a candidate, while the series of questions and the proposed test are Fangrong's.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Qiran Zhi: In a hall sermon requested by the layman Lü Yinghui and other visitors, Qiran Chaozhi says that delight in scenery can become attachment as soon as choosing and rejecting arise. He explicitly introduces the complete verse as spoken by the World-Honored One at the assembly on complete discernment. Qiran then tells the gathered laypeople that their differing practices, including precept keeping and Chan inquiry, still fall within the circle he is discussing. ClaimAnchors.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Monk Tianyin: In a letter to the layman Cao Nianzi, Tianyin Yuanxiu responds to repeated reports of suffering. He says that rich and poor alike are caught in trouble, then quotes the Buddha's complete Diamond Sutra verse about conditioned things as dreams, illusions, bubbles, shadows, dew, and lightning. Tianyin applies the quotation to body and mind, rank, wealth, and affliction: seeing their lack of fixed reality lets one act amid ordinary demands without being mastered by them. The verse is the Buddha's inherited speech; the explanation and advice to Cao are Tianyin's own.

ClaimAnchors.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Poshan: In Poshan Haiming's hall sermon, a monk first asks about the true character of things and receives a blow. Poshan then tells the assembly that he had dreamed of lay visitors Yin and Dai asking him to preach. He calls family, property, official rank, awakening, and even release dreams before quoting the complete Buddha verse. Poshan immediately asks what an open-eyed dream is, leaving the assembly without an answer. When Yin later kneels and asks him to explain, Poshan strikes him and withdraws. The citation starts the live test; the blow is Poshan's response, not part of the Buddha's verse.

ClaimAnchors.AttributionNote: Expanded Record of Chan Master Cishou Huaishen: In Cishou Huaishen's hall sermon, the Buddha's complete verse is recited first: conditioned things are to be seen as dreams, illusions, bubbles, and shadows. Cishou then turns the instruction into his own question: if that is how conditioned things are viewed, how should the unconditioned be viewed? His answer invokes an obstruction in the eye that even a skilled physician cannot pick out. ClaimAnchors.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Fangrongxi: In a short instruction, Fangrong Ruxi asks what the 'king of the teaching who breaks existence' actually reveals. He tries several familiar doctrinal verses as possible answers, including the complete Diamond Sutra verse with these dream, illusion, bubble, and shadow images. Each is framed as 'Could it be this?' Fangrong says that merely answering in that way would let talkative teachers borrow the title without showing their own understanding. He closes by saying the wooden elder, his staff, will have to test anyone claiming more. The verse is inherited Buddha speech raised as a candidate, while the series of questions and the proposed test are Fangrong's.

Senses.Explanation: The Buddha's Diamond Sutra verse compares conditioned things to a dream, illusion, bubble, and shadow, then adds dew and lightning. Six later Chan records quote the same line in different settings: Tianyin counsels a suffering layman, Poshan turns it into a live test, Cishou asks about the unconditioned, Fangrong questions borrowed formulas, Huijue applies it at a memorial, and Qiran addresses lay visitors. In each witness, the verse's original speaker differs from the named master who raises and applies it.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J23/J23nB134.xml). Recorded Sayings of the Five Houses (Selections). Yunmen Wenyan is invited to a meal by the official Chen Shangshu, who asks what a traveling monk’s work is beyond Confucian books and scriptural specialists. Yunmen turns the question back: what is the teaching’s intent beyond colored scrolls and words that fall silent? When Chen cannot answer, Yunmen asks whether he reads the Lotus Sūtra, quotes its line that all livelihoods and productive work do not conflict with reality, and asks how many inhabitants of the neither-perception-nor-nonperception heaven lose their place. Chen again falls silent and bows after Yunmen warns him against a hasty claim to understanding. The headword is an explicitly marked scriptural quotation inside Yunmen’s test, not Chen’s answer or a standalone endorsement of every job.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J25/J25nB171.xml). Recorded Sayings of Monk Tianyin. Tianyin Yuanxiu retells Yunmen’s same exchange with Chen Shangshu and inserts his own comments between its turns. Where Chen is pressed about the teaching beyond scrolls, Tianyin proposes a sharper answer he would give in Chen’s place. After Yunmen quotes the Lotus livelihood line and asks about the highest formless heaven, Tianyin again supplies a hypothetical reply, then says Yunmen wielded a keen sword and Chen had to submit to its testing. The exact headword remains the Lotus wording quoted by Yunmen in the old case; Tianyin’s present action is to appraise and recast the official’s missed responses, not to author a new scriptural saying.

Occurrences.Kwic: 言須會宗，勿自立規矩。舉：雲門到江州，陳操尚書請齋，纔見便問：「儒書中即不問，三乘十二分教自有座主，作麼生是衲僧行腳事？」門曰：「曾問幾人來？」曰：「即今問上座。」門曰：「即今且置，作麼生是教意？」曰：「黃卷赤軸。」門曰：「這箇是文字語言，作麼生是教意？」曰：「口欲談而辭喪，心欲緣而慮忘。」門曰：「口欲談而辭喪，為對有言；心欲緣而慮忘，為對妄想。作麼生是教意？」書無語。門曰：「見說尚書看《法華經》，是否？」曰：「是。」門曰：「經中道：『一切治生產業，皆與實相不相違背。』且道非非想天有幾人退位？」書無語。門曰：「尚書且莫艸艸，三經五論，師僧拋卻，特入叢林，十年二十年尚不奈何，尚書又爭得會？」書禮拜曰：「某甲罪過。」無著頌作家慣戰不齎糧，奪鼓攙旗勢莫當。虎驟龍驤誰辦的，反思仁義勝剛強。玅湛頌調將埋兵幾戰征，尚書空使口頭爭。三千劍客今何在，嬴得悲風動地生。靈瑞頌袖裏金鎚劈面來，左旋右轉趁風雷。韶陽因謗斯經故，直得披毛戴角回。舉：法眼聞齋魚，問僧：「還聞麼？適來若聞，如今不聞；如今若聞，適來不聞。」無著頌

Occurrences.Kwic: 中會取，直透萬重關，不住青霄中。先了却那邊，却須這邊行履。何故？不因今日事，爭話昨夜夢？恁麼參到徹取，而自由自在。衲僧若未然，爭奈喫鐵棒何？還吾平生粥飯來。故經曰：若不見佛知見，未出凡夫境；若悟入佛知見，不出三界出。貪嗔痴一句，了然道著，分明許你作大活計。畢竟還恁麼也，公私分曉。長安道：示眾曰：大乘妙法蓮華經，字字含玄感應新。舉起一卷玉軸，則瞿曇鼻孔人人皆収手裡；拈取一經太意，則諸佛正眼箇箇悉在心中。絲毫許無移易，毛髮許無滲漏。故經曰：一切治生產業，皆與實相不相違背。若恁麼，大地有情悉是同時成道作佛去。且道誰人如此？頭長三尺，頸短二寸。示眾曰：教意親參，祖意正到。祖意親參，教意正到。祖教不二，意句無別。雖然與麼，實到此田地始得。若未到，切忌舉教拈祖，知趣能有幾人？故經曰：此眾無枝葉，唯有諸貞實。增上慢人，退亦佳矣。若然，向上一路，千聖不傳，是向上人而應辨得。初心未改，還同後心，則又何愁不會？人人須是發悟。諸佛中未了漢名眾生，眾生中了義漢名諸佛。所以達磨大師曰：直指人心，見性成佛。如何是正？當恁麼時
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X72/X72n1428.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Jingci Huihui. In a separate recorded sermon, Zide Huihui praises the Lotus Sūtra as a teaching whose words point toward the Buddha’s own seeing. He explicitly cites its line that all livelihoods and productive work do not conflict with reality, then says that, taken through, all sentient beings would awaken together. He asks who could meet that claim and answers with a deliberately odd bodily image before moving to the relation between scriptural and ancestral intent. The retained words belong to the scripture as quoted by Zide; his current sermon tests how to realize them rather than treating the mere fact of working as sufficient.

Senses.Explanation: The Lotus Sūtra says that ordinary livelihoods and productive work need not stand apart from reality. Yunmen Wenyan is invited to a meal by the official Chen Shangshu, who asks what a traveling monk’s work is beyond Confucian books and scriptural specialists. Yunmen turns the question back: what is the teaching’s intent beyond colored scrolls and words that fall silent? When Chen cannot answer, Yunmen asks whether he reads the Lotus Sūtra, quotes its line that all livelihoods and productive work do not conflict with reality, and asks how many inhabitants of the neither-perception-nor-nonperception heaven lose their place. Chen again falls silent and bows after Yunmen warns him against a hasty claim to understanding. The headword is an explicitly marked scriptural quotation inside Yunmen’s test, not Chen’s answer or a standalone endorsement of every job. Tianyin Yuanxiu retells Yunmen’s same exchange with Chen Shangshu and inserts his own comments between its turns. Where Chen is pressed about the teaching beyond scrolls, Tianyin proposes a sharper answer he would give in Chen’s place. After Yunmen quotes the Lotus livelihood line and asks about the highest formless heaven, Tianyin again supplies a hypothetical reply, then says Yunmen wielded a keen sword and Chen had to submit to its testing. The exact headword remains the Lotus wording quoted by Yunmen in the old case; Tianyin’s present action is to appraise and recast the official’s missed responses, not to author a new scriptural saying. A case collection repeats the Yunmen–Chen Shangshu encounter in full, including Yunmen’s explicit Lotus quotation and Chen’s failure to answer the follow-up question about beings in the highest formless heaven. Those poems show later reactions to the case but do not make the verse writers the speakers of the retained Lotus line. This is a parallel transport of the same old exchange, not an independent new encounter. Occurrences.Kwic: 各由見解深淺。不以調與不調之行而定法義。偏圓但自隨病對治。不須讚此毀彼二密意破相顯性教說前教中所變之境既皆虛妄。能變之識豈獨真實。心境互依空而似有故也。且心不孤起。託境方生。境不自生。由心故現。心空即境謝。境滅即心空。未有無境之心。曾無無心之境。如夢見物似能見所見之殊。其實同一虛妄都無所有。諸識諸境亦復如是。以皆假託眾緣無自性故。未曾有一法不從因緣生。是故一切法無不是空者。凡所有相皆是虛妄。是故空中無色。無眼耳鼻舌身意。無十八界。無十二因緣。無四諦。無智。亦無得。無業。無報。無修。無證。生死涅槃平等如幻。但以不住一切無執無著而為道行。諸部般若千餘卷經。及中百門等。三論廣百論等。皆說此也此教與禪門泯絕無寄宗全同。既同世尊所說菩薩所弘。云何漸門禪主及講習之徒。每聞此說。即謗云。撥無因果。佛自云。無業無報。豈邪見乎。若云佛說此言自有深意者。豈禪門此說無深意耶。若云我曾推徵覺無深意者。自是汝遇不解之流。但可嫌人。豈可斥法。此上一教據佛本意雖不相違。

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X69/X69n1344.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Sixin Wuxin (Huanglong Four Houses Record, No. 3). In the Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Sixin Wuxin, a lay magistrate identified only as Duan sends Sixin a verse that asks: if all phenomena are unborn, how could a mind die? Sixin answers in a separate verse that just because phenomena are unborn, the mind has long been dead, and asks the addressee to cut off even the finest trace. Senses.Note: The pair states that all phenomena neither arise nor cease. Foyuan challenges a merely inherited repetition; Huiyue and Tianran apply it to changing appearances. Shanduo, Jifei, and Qibai make it the opening of separate present teachings before adding images or questions. The second clause is needed: nonarising alone can sound like absence, while the paired source turns continue to show events and responses.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J37/J37nB371.xml). In an evening talk Foyuan Chegang announces that all phenomena neither arise nor cease, then rebukes old Gautama for calling gold iron and jokes that Bodhidharma had nowhere to hide but went east. He offers the same tiny coin whether anyone can strike down these two old masters or cannot, then ends with frost and snow images. The pair is Foyuan's present, deliberately provocative opening; the later Yunmen case in the same KWIC is a separate example, not its speaker.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J38/J38nB418.xml). On his first evening at Ganlu, Huiyue Xu says many streams enter one sea and diverse things enter one true teaching. He voices the paired line, extends it with neither existence nor nonexistence, and immediately names mountains, light and dark, sentient and insentient things as endlessly speaking. Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J38/J38nB406.xml). At a bathing-the-Buddha sermon, Tianran Hanshi says all phenomena neither arise nor cease, yet appear as conditions gather, like flowers in a mirror or the moon in water. He raises his staff and asks the assembly whether they see the Buddha passing before their own faces, then strikes the staff and asks whether they hear. His visible and audible demonstrations make the pair a question about how appearances are met, not a claim that nothing can be seen or heard.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J38/J38nB414.xml). In a teaching after returning to Donglin, Shanduo Zhenzai voices the pair, then points to the mountain outside, rain striking pear blossoms, and butterflies flying. A monk immediately asks what Buddha is and what lies beyond Buddha; Shanduo answers first with a scorched seed that cannot sprout, then with changing clouds and a downpour. The opening pair belongs to Shanduo's present teaching, and the following questions test it against ordinary sights and the monk's categories.

In an evening talk Foyuan Chegang announces that all phenomena neither arise nor cease, then rebukes old Gautama for calling gold iron and jokes that Bodhidharma had nowhere to hide but went east. He offers the same tiny coin whether anyone can strike down these two old masters or cannot, then ends with frost and snow images. The pair is Foyuan's present, deliberately provocative opening; the later Yunmen case in the same KWIC is a separate example, not its speaker.

ClaimAnchors.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J38/J38nB418.xml). On his first evening at Ganlu, Huiyue Xu says many streams enter one sea and diverse things enter one true teaching. ClaimAnchors.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J38/J38nB406.xml). At a bathing-the-Buddha sermon, Tianran Hanshi says all phenomena neither arise nor cease, yet appear as conditions gather, like flowers in a mirror or the moon in water. Senses.Explanation: All phenomena neither arise nor cease: six teachers voice this paired line while meeting appearances, questions, and their own listeners. In an evening talk Foyuan Chegang announces that all phenomena neither arise nor cease, then rebukes old Gautama for calling gold iron and jokes that Bodhidharma had nowhere to hide but went east. He offers the same tiny coin whether anyone can strike down these two old masters or cannot, then ends with frost and snow images. The pair is Foyuan's present, deliberately provocative opening; the later Yunmen case in the same KWIC is a separate example, not its speaker. On his first evening at Ganlu, Huiyue Xu says many streams enter one sea and diverse things enter one true teaching. He voices the paired line, extends it with neither existence nor nonexistence, and immediately names mountains, light and dark, sentient and insentient things as endlessly speaking. He asks the brothers whether they hear this and answers that the Buddha seals the direct root while he cannot seek it by plucking leaves and twigs. Here the pair holds equality and the visible variety together in his current address. At a bathing-the-Buddha sermon, Tianran Hanshi says all phenomena neither arise nor cease, yet appear as conditions gather, like flowers in a mirror or the moon in water. He raises his staff and asks the assembly whether they see the Buddha passing before their own faces, then strikes the staff and asks whether they hear. His visible and audible demonstrations make the pair a question about how appearances are met, not a claim that nothing can be seen or heard. Senses.Explanation: The line from the morning star: how strange — all beings are endowed with the thus-come one's wisdom and virtue-marks, only by deluded thinking and clinging do they fail to attain it. The whisk at Baishan's hall hears it and laughs out loud — quite right, very apt — yet dares guarantee the old brother is not through. The telling and the plain price: Dahui Zonggao tells it whole — before the mountain of right awakening the morning star appeared and Shakyamuni suddenly woke; at the place he had verified he saw the great earth and all beings of one body with him, equal, and said the line: what I verified, the ten directions' buddhas and even the wriggling creatures attained all at once — and he set the ocean-seal at each person's heel; Huanyou Zhengchuan reads it round and empty — I observe all beings are endowed with the thus-come one's wisdom and virtue-marks but by deluded thinking and clinging do not verify it; with no clinging, is that not empty? — the Diamond's beings-beings are no beings beside it; Muyun Tongmen preaches the plain price — what is deluded thinking? just forgetting this one great matter; touch any place blankly and all one does and makes is deluded thinking; Zhu'an Zhenyan has his staff report it in a loud voice — the yellow-faced old man deep on the snow ridge lifted his head at midnight, suddenly saw the morning star, made much ado and said the line — and before the sound had ended: one film over the eye, sky-flowers falling in profusion — a slap of the staff. The halls that doubt it: Binya Jian grants the whole mechanism wholly bared, the root cut through — yet inspected closely, very much like stamping from a mold; Zishui writes to a layman — the old man of the snow mountain's one piece of bitter heart is to make people wake on the spot, but people simply will not: they neglect the ordinary and hurry to seek the lofty and deep, how lamentable; Baishan Dekai lifts the whisk — the yellow-faced one on the whisk-tip enters right settledness, sees the morning star, wakes, says the line — and the whisk cannot help laughing, crying quite right, very apt, yet I dare guarantee the old brother is not through.

Entries.SourceTerm: 一切眾生具有如來智慧德相，但以妄想執著而不證得

Senses.PreferredTarget: All beings have the Tathagata’s wisdom and qualities, yet deluded thoughts and clinging keep them from realizing it
SearchAliases: all beings have the tathagata’s wisdom and qualities, yet deluded thoughts and clinging keep them from realizing it
Senses.Note: The Buddha’s awakening statement says that all beings have the Tathagata’s wisdom and qualities but do not realize them because of deluded thought and clinging. Muyun uses it to urge his listeners to turn from worldly status toward the matter already present. Baichi explains the two halves in counsel to a laywoman, contrasting a constant light with habits of following sights and sounds. Baiyu quotes the statement on the Buddha’s awakening day, then asks whether the Buddha’s own movements could be called clinging too. Yuan’an goes further, questioning a fixed division between wisdom to gain and delusion to discard. The later sermons keep the original statement alive by testing what it means to possess yet not realize.

Occurrences.Kwic: 呵罵人，便道如夜叉羅剎難于親近。不見汾陽示眾云：『汾陽門下有西河獅子，當門踞坐，但有來者，即便咬殺。有何方便入得汾陽門，得見汾陽人？若見汾陽人，堪與佛祖為師；不見汾陽人，盡是立地死漢。』」再住破山。師云：「明日開爐，今日普說。當初釋迦老子在法華會上說，十方三世諸佛皆以一大事因緣故，出現于世。此一大事，在諸佛甚是圓滿，諸人也不曾欠缺在。諸佛甚是靈明，諸人也不曾遮蔽。此便是普說底意。所以差別者何？記得黃面老子在雪山頂上，嘆曰：『奇哉！奇哉！一切眾生具有如來智慧德相，但以妄想執著而不證得。』且如何是妄想？但忘卻此一大事，觸處茫然，所作所為皆妄想也。縱然位至君侯，最為榮貴，皆是生死邊事。所以諸佛興慈運悲，出世來提持你，使你知有此大事，不做眾生。然此妄想無始以來綿結牢固，即使巨靈神斧子亦斬不開，天大將軍亦難下手，只在當人憤發，起猛利念頭，自省自愧。既此一大事，我與諸佛無殊，如何讓他做佛，我做眾生？讓他人成聖成賢，而我甘處凡愚下劣？有此一念，歷劫妄想便可消融，便是生死海中轉頭時節。既能轉頭，又要尊師重法。古來學人遇見知識，生

Muyun then explains delusion as forgetting that matter amid ordinary activity and urges each listener to turn and examine himself. Occurrences.Kwic: 胡深旨。羅山云：「我這裏秪有一口劍，劍下有分身之意，亦有出身之路。」快哉斯言，知音者少，隨氀𣯜趁，大隊漢烏足以語此哉。示超奇善友示超奇善友人非生知，貴在力學，學而計之時日、積之歲月，未有不成者。設或一暴十寒，吾知其不能進矣。參禪亦然，時而鞭策，日而揣摩，歲月無虛度之功，終身有實證之驗。祖翁田地，四至契書，一一分明、一一了當，名為絕學，無為閒道人也。雖然無為無事人，猶是金鎖難，且道：節角在什麼處？試下一轉語看。示超慧陳氏夫人示超慧陳氏夫人一切眾生具有如來智慧德相，但以妄想執著而不證得，此是黃面瞿曇初證初得時大開口縫，為今古人立箇定案也。何名智慧德相？即當人一點常光，照天照地，最微最妙，至虛至靈，不可思議境界是也。何名妄想執著？即當人日用之中隨聲逐色，恣縱虛妄，胡思亂想，不可遏滅境界是也。妄想無暫停、執著無暫解，智慧德相如何得現前透露乎？所以善知識見人問著，不論是男、是女，便與劈頭拈出，宿有靈根底直下知歸，更不在絮絮忉忉。其或未能領略「父母未生前，如何是我本來面目」，且將這箇話端向行住坐臥處密密提撕，刻刻窮究，無絲毫
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J28/J28nB202.xml). The Buddha is the quoted speaker; Baichi applies both halves of the sentence to this named student's practice.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J36/J36nB359.xml). On the Buddha's enlightenment day, Baiyu Jingsi recounts Shakyamuni seeing the morning star and quotes his exclamation that all beings have the Tathagata's wisdom but fail to realize it because of deluded thought and attachment. Baiyu immediately shouts and challenges the statement: he asks whether the Buddha's departure from home, awakening and many teachings would themselves count as deluded activity. He then favors eating when hungry and dressing when cold. The headword remains the Buddha's reported utterance; Baiyu uses it as the target of his provocative current sermon, not as his own unqualified doctrine.

Occurrences.Kwic: 第三喝，不惟海祖無處轉身，直教再參三十年；當時者僧若下得第四喝，豈止馬師不敢口轆轆地說白道黑，免得後代兒孫遞相鈍置。諸兄弟！僼上座恁麼出脫，古人還知者四喝落處麼？若知得者四喝落處，說甚麼臨濟大師一喝如金剛王寶劍、一喝如踞地獅子、一喝如探竿影艸、一喝不作一喝用，是甚熱碗鳴聲？設或未然，莫道僼上座無相為好。」復喝一喝，下座。佛成道日，秉拂。「大道絕遮欄，其誰趣向？虛空無背面，何處雕鐫？昔日釋迦老子于正覺山中夜睹明星，豁然大悟，便云：『奇哉！一切眾生具有如來智慧德相，但以妄想執著而不證得。』者箇老古錐、徐六擔板只見一邊，殊不知，一切諸佛皆以妄想執著而有如來智慧德相可證。若有如來智慧德相可證，則是眾生妄想執著；若除眾生妄想執著，則無如來智慧德相可證；既無如來智慧德相可證，則內無所證；既無眾生妄想執著可除，則外無所修；外無所修，則無眾生可度；內無所證，則無諸佛可成；既無諸佛可成，亦無眾生可度，則一道平等，浩然大均。現前若僧、若俗，若男、若女，若艸木、若叢林，若山河大地、若日月星辰，無不同一眼見、同一耳聞、同一心知、同一受用

Entries.SourceTerm: 一切眾生性清淨，從本無生無可滅。即此身心是幻生，幻化之中無罪福

Senses.PreferredTarget: All beings are pure by nature, unborn and undying from the start. This body and mind are a phantom arising; within the phantom there is no fixed sin or merit.
AlternateTargets: The nature of all beings is pure, without birth or extinction; body and mind arise as illusion, where sin and merit have no fixed substance.
SearchAliases: Kasyapa Buddha on pure nature and phantom body

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X66/X66n1298.xml). Gāthās and Verses of the Chan Gate’s Patriarchs. The verse anthology places these four lines under Kasyapa Buddha in the traditional sequence of seven Buddhas: beings are pure in nature and originally unborn, while this body and mind arise like an apparition with no fixed wrongdoing or merit within it. The surrounding verses similarly treat embodied forms and action as insubstantial. The named speaker is a traditional attribution supplied by this Chinese transmission sequence, not an independently verified historical speech. On its own this witness states the verse without a present question and reply; the later applications are needed to show how teachers qualify and use its closing denial.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X68/X68n1318.xml). Continued Essentials from the Sayings of Ancient Worthies. Letan Ying quotes the complete verse as an ancestor's saying, then calls it remarkable but still compares relying on it to discomfort after too much food or sitting too long. Even passing the ancestral barrier may leave countless layers. Better than leaning at another's door and looking toward another mountain is to sit by the fire with a worthy person; but how is the ancestral barrier discussed there? After a pause he gives snow across mountains and a freezing ape breaking a dead branch. The exact verse belongs to the traditional Kasyapa attribution, while the present teacher refuses to let its correct-sounding purity settle the listener's work.

Occurrences.Kwic: 佛國土，富有法財，非求報也。昔摩訶迦葉尊者，為煆金師，善明金性，使其柔伏。付法傳云：甞於久遠劫中，毗婆尸佛涅槃後，四眾起墖。墖中像面，金色有缺壞。時有貧女，將金珠往金師所，請飾佛面。既而因共發願：願我二人，為無姻夫婦。以是因緣，九十一劫，身皆金色。後生梵天，天壽盡，生中天摩竭陀國婆羅門家，名曰迦葉波，此云飲光勝尊，葢以金色為號也。繇是志求出家，冀度諸有。佛言：善來比丘！鬚髮自除，袈裟著體，常於眾中稱歎第一，乃至付法傳衣，為西天初祖。此因果歷然，以嚴飾金故，而得身有金光；以願力相資，而證極果。此不求報而報自至，非求報也。余甞評之：菩提心如種子，福如雨露良田，惡如火𦦨刀斧。假如種苗生發之時，必得其雨露水土，方可成就；或遭其火燒刀斫，又安可植耶？如成棟梁之材，刀斧俱非，水土亦無用矣。七佛偈曰：起諸善法本是幻，造諸惡業亦是幻。身如聚沫心如風，幻出無根無實性。愚者謂善惡俱幻，造諸惡業，似不相妨。殊不知幻人相織幻輪圍，幻業能招幻所治。又云：一切眾生性清淨，從本無生無可滅。即此身心是幻生，幻化之中無罪福。如成棟梁，則不用刀斧水土。如佛成道時，無邊剎土，萬德莊嚴，皆自心現量，悉無始已來善根之所成就。故云：報圓極果豈非報？但因地中無求報之心耳。世間人所行善惡，毫髮不爽。昔西域一樵夫，賣柴於市中，逢一僧將賣錢，悉皆施與，遂此施心，歡喜無量，行廿餘里，捨此報身，後生人道，為大富長者，其廿餘里金銀寶藏，自然湧出。斯施利甚微，而施心勝，故感報亦勝。以此觀之，不求福報，不可不作福。如不作福，生世貧窮，為人役使，良可悲夫。或有引達磨大師初見武帝時，帝問曰：朕即位已來，造寺、寫經、度僧，不可勝紀，有何功德？祖曰：並無功德。帝曰：何以無功德？祖曰：此但人天小果，有漏之因，如影隨形，雖有非實。帝曰：如何是真功德？祖曰：淨智玅圓，體自空寂，如是功德，不以世求。斯皆深達法性入理之談，豈可以修行分中，而廢其因果耶？如未成佛時，人天小果而不修者，是智耶？愚耶？國王、大臣，人小果也；梵王、帝釋，天小果也。此無殊因，焉有勝報？但隨業緣受之，非求報也。然自心之因，自心之果，如貪報地獄，嗔報餓鬼，癡報畜生，善惡相雜，報以修羅，五戒人身，十善天道。財施者，捨慳貪而得富；法施者，適機感以傳燈。此種種報緣，而有差別，非心外之境也。釋疑品第九釋疑品第九問：信心不具大愚

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X72/X72n1435.xml). Expanded Record of Chan Master Wuyi Yuanlai. Wuyi Yuanlai uses the verse in a sustained argument about generosity and consequences. He first compares the awakening mind to a seed that needs rain and good soil and can be destroyed by fire and blades. People who hear that good and bad actions are illusory may wrongly suppose harmful action does not matter, although illusory deeds still bring illusory suffering. He then quotes Kasyapa's verse and compares complete attainment to finished timber no longer needing the tools that shaped it. Not seeking reward does not mean refusing to do good. The inherited verse therefore cannot be used as the teacher's permission to dismiss cause and consequence during practice.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X72/X72n1441.xml). Dharma Assembly Record at Yunshan of Chan Master Weilin. Weilin Daopei introduces several traditionally attributed Buddha verses as breaking the two fixations on body and mind. He explicitly names Kasyapa before this verse and explains that pure nature is originally without birth and death, while body, mind, wrongdoing and merit cannot be grasped as fixed entities. He then warns that ordinary people who recognize faults and repent can improve, whereas those who deny their faults continue creating harmful deeds. The traditional speaker and Weilin's present explanation remain distinct. The denial of fixed wrongdoing and merit is thus paired locally with responsibility for conduct, not presented as proof that every action is equivalent.

ClaimAnchors.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X66/X66n1298.xml). Gāthās and Verses of the Chan Gate’s Patriarchs. The verse anthology places these four lines under Kasyapa Buddha in the traditional sequence of seven Buddhas: beings are pure in nature and originally unborn, while this body and mind arise like an apparition with no fixed wrongdoing or merit within it. The surrounding verses similarly treat embodied forms and action as insubstantial. The named speaker is a traditional attribution supplied by this Chinese transmission sequence, not an independently verified historical speech. On its own this witness states the verse without a present question and reply; the later applications are needed to show how teachers qualify and use its closing denial.

ClaimAnchors.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X68/X68n1318.xml). Continued Essentials from the Sayings of Ancient Worthies. Letan Ying quotes the complete verse as an ancestor's saying, then calls it remarkable but still compares relying on it to discomfort after too much food or sitting too long. Even passing the ancestral barrier may leave countless layers. Better than leaning at another's door and looking toward another mountain is to sit by the fire with a worthy person; but how is the ancestral barrier discussed there? After a pause he gives snow across mountains and a freezing ape breaking a dead branch. The exact verse belongs to the traditional Kasyapa attribution, while the present teacher refuses to let its correct-sounding purity settle the listener's work.

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 佛國土，富有法財，非求報也。昔摩訶迦葉尊者，為煆金師，善明金性，使其柔伏。付法傳云：甞於久遠劫中，毗婆尸佛涅槃後，四眾起墖。墖中像面，金色有缺壞。時有貧女，將金珠往金師所，請飾佛面。既而因共發願：願我二人，為無姻夫婦。以是因緣，九十一劫，身皆金色。後生梵天，天壽盡，生中天摩竭陀國婆羅門家，名曰迦葉波，此云飲光勝尊，葢以金色為號也。繇是志求出家，冀度諸有。佛言：善來比丘！鬚髮自除，袈裟著體，常於眾中稱歎第一，乃至付法傳衣，為西天初祖。此因果歷然，以嚴飾金故，而得身有金光；以願力相資，而證極果。此不求報而報自至，非求報也。余甞評之：菩提心如種子，福如雨露良田，惡如火𦦨刀斧。假如種苗生發之時，必得其雨露水土，方可成就；或遭其火燒刀斫，又安可植耶？如成棟梁之材，刀斧俱非，水土亦無用矣。七佛偈曰：起諸善法本是幻，造諸惡業亦是幻。身如聚沫心如風，幻出無根無實性。愚者謂善惡俱幻，造諸惡業，似不相妨。殊不知幻人相織幻輪圍，幻業能招幻所治。又云：一切眾生性清淨，從本無生無可滅。即此身心是幻生，幻化之中無罪福。如成棟梁，則不用刀斧水土。如佛成道時，無邊剎土，萬德莊嚴，皆自心現量，悉無始已來善根之所成就。故云：報圓極果豈非報？但因地中無求報之心耳。世間人所行善惡，毫髮不爽。昔西域一樵夫，賣柴於市中，逢一僧將賣錢，悉皆施與，遂此施心，歡喜無量，行廿餘里，捨此報身，後生人道，為大富長者，其廿餘里金銀寶藏，自然湧出。斯施利甚微，而施心勝，故感報亦勝。以此觀之，不求福報，不可不作福。如不作福，生世貧窮，為人役使，良可悲夫。或有引達磨大師初見武帝時，帝問曰：朕即位已來，造寺、寫經、度僧，不可勝紀，有何功德？祖曰：並無功德。帝曰：何以無功德？祖曰：此但人天小果，有漏之因，如影隨形，雖有非實。帝曰：如何是真功德？祖曰：淨智玅圓，體自空寂，如是功德，不以世求。斯皆深達法性入理之談，豈可以修行分中，而廢其因果耶？如未成佛時，人天小果而不修者，是智耶？愚耶？國王、大臣，人小果也；梵王、帝釋，天小果也。此無殊因，焉有勝報？但隨業緣受之，非求報也。然自心之因，自心之果，如貪報地獄，嗔報餓鬼，癡報畜生，善惡相雜，報以修羅，五戒人身，十善天道。財施者，捨慳貪而得富；法施者，適機感以傳燈。此種種報緣，而有差別，非心外之境也。釋疑品第九釋疑品第九問：信心不具大愚

ClaimAnchors.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X72/X72n1435.xml). Expanded Record of Chan Master Wuyi Yuanlai. Wuyi Yuanlai uses the verse in a sustained argument about generosity and consequences. He first compares the awakening mind to a seed that needs rain and good soil and can be destroyed by fire and blades. People who hear that good and bad actions are illusory may wrongly suppose harmful action does not matter, although illusory deeds still bring illusory suffering. He then quotes Kasyapa's verse and compares complete attainment to finished timber no longer needing the tools that shaped it. Not seeking reward does not mean refusing to do good. The inherited verse therefore cannot be used as the teacher's permission to dismiss cause and consequence during practice.

Senses.Explanation: The verse anthology places these four lines under Kasyapa Buddha in the traditional sequence of seven Buddhas: beings are pure in nature and originally unborn, while this body and mind arise like an apparition with no fixed wrongdoing or merit within it. The surrounding verses similarly treat embodied forms and action as insubstantial. The named speaker is a traditional attribution supplied by this Chinese transmission sequence, not an independently verified historical speech. On its own this witness states the verse without a present question and reply; the later applications are needed to show how teachers qualify and use its closing denial. Letan Ying quotes the complete verse as an ancestor's saying, then calls it remarkable but still compares relying on it to discomfort after too much food or sitting too long. Even passing the ancestral barrier may leave countless layers. Better than leaning at another's door and looking toward another mountain is to sit by the fire with a worthy person; but how is the ancestral barrier discussed there? After a pause he gives snow across mountains and a freezing ape breaking a dead branch. The exact verse belongs to the traditional Kasyapa attribution, while the present teacher refuses to let its correct-sounding purity settle the listener's work. Wuyi Yuanlai uses the verse in a sustained argument about generosity and consequences. He first compares the awakening mind to a seed that needs rain and good soil and can be destroyed by fire and blades. People who hear that good and bad actions are illusory may wrongly suppose harmful action does not matter, although illusory deeds still bring illusory suffering. He then quotes Kasyapa's verse and compares complete attainment to finished timber no longer needing the tools that shaped it. Not seeking reward does not mean refusing to do good. The inherited verse therefore cannot be used as the teacher's permission to dismiss cause and consequence during practice. Senses.Explanation: All sentient beings have Buddha-nature is a universal proposition that Zen records repeatedly place in the mouth of a questioner confronting Zhaozhou’s “no” about a dog. Its recurring job is not to close the issue by an inherited teaching but to sharpen a public contradiction: if the universal statement stands, why does Zhaozhou deny the dog? Later masters raise, redirect, or refuse that collision rather than supplying one uniform reconciliation.

Senses.Note: An unnamed monk asks Dasui why a tortoise has bone outside its skin when other creatures have skin outside their bones; Dasui covers the tortoise with a straw sandal. Hengchuan and Yongjue each later quote that question and make distinct verse comments. Entries.SourceTerm: 一切萬法不離自性，何期自性本自清淨

Senses.PreferredTarget: All phenomena remain within self-nature; who expected self-nature to be pure from the start?
AlternateTargets: Nothing in the myriad phenomena is apart from self-nature; unexpectedly, it is originally clear.
SearchAliases: all phenomena within self-nature, originally pure
Senses.Note: Huineng voices realization before the Fifth Patriarch; Chaozong Tongren later cites the same words to ask why a single sutra line brought insight on two occasions.

Occurrences.Kwic: 一條拄杖，為甚前面道『為他途路不得力』，後面道『楖栗橫擔不顧人，直入千峰萬峰去』？又如五祖演舉趙州柏樹子話云：『如何是祖師西來意？庭前柏樹子。恁麼會便不是了也。如何是祖師西來意？庭前柏樹子。恁麼會方始得。』只是一箇柏樹子，因甚前面道『恁麼會便不是了也』，後面道『恁麼會方始得』？此在法不在人者，一等是箇時節，因甚有得有不得？又如六祖初聞應無所住而生其心，即便開悟，作偈云：『菩提本無樹，明鏡亦非臺，本來無一物，何處惹塵埃？』後至五祖室中，復徵至應無所住而生其心，言下大徹，乃云：『一切萬法不離自性，何期自性本自清淨？何期自性本不生滅？何期自性本自具足？何期自性本無動搖？何期自性能生萬法？』此在人不在法者。試問諸人：只是一箇應無所住而生其心，因甚前面也從此悟、後面也從此悟？前面悟時便恁麼道、後面悟時又不恁麼道？又如龐公問石頭：『不與萬法為侶者是甚麼人？』石頭以手掩其口即開悟。又問馬祖：『不與萬法為侶者是甚麼人？』祖云：『待汝一口吸盡西江水即向你道。』言下大徹。也是如此。諸人當知，綱宗一透，所謂一句通，千句百句一時通；一機透，千機百機一時透。你若會得趙州道水淺不是泊船處底消息，便會得祥菴主
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J34/J34nB300.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Chaozong. Chaozong Tongren compares Huineng's first awakening on hearing the Diamond Sutra line about not abiding with a later, fuller breakthrough when the Fifth Patriarch repeats it. He quotes Huineng's words that all phenomena remain within self-nature and that self-nature is pure from the start, then asks why the same sutra line yielded two different moments. Huineng is the exact quoted speaker; Chaozong uses the quote to challenge the assembly.

Occurrences.Kwic: ，以為教門。然以無上微妙祕密圓明真實正法眼藏，付於上首大迦葉尊者，展轉傳授二十八世，至達摩屆於此土，得可大師承襲，以至於我。今以法寶及所傳袈裟，用付於汝，善自保護，無令斷絕。聽吾偈曰：有情來下種，因地果還生。無情既無種，無性亦無生。盧跪受訖，問：法則既受，衣付何人？祖曰：昔達摩初至，人未之信，故傳衣以明得法。今信心已熟，衣乃爭端，止於汝身，不復傳也。六祖慧能大師六祖慧能大師祖抵黃梅，參禮五祖，當呈偈後，三鼓入五祖室。五祖復徵其初悟應無所住而生其心語，祖於言下大徹，遂啟五祖曰：一切萬法不離自性，何期自性本自清淨？何期自性本不生滅？何期自性本自具足？何期自性本無動搖？何期自性能生萬法？五祖知悟本性，謂祖曰：不識本心，學法無益；若識本心，見自本性，即名丈夫．天人師．佛。遂傳衣法。五祖送祖至九江驛邊，令祖上船，祖隨即把櫓，五祖曰：合是吾渡汝。祖曰：迷時師度，悟時自度，度名雖一，用處不同。能蒙師傳法，今已得悟，只合自性自度。五祖云：如是，如是。以後佛法由汝大行。祖至廣州法性寺，值印宗法師講涅槃經，寓止廊廡間。暮夜風颺剎旛，聞二僧對論，一曰旛動，一曰風動，往復不已。祖曰：不是風動，不是旛動，
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X68/X68n1319.xml). Imperially Selected Recorded Sayings. In the record's Sixth Patriarch section, the Fifth Patriarch repeats the Diamond Sutra line to Huineng in his room. Huineng then tells him that all phenomena remain within self-nature and expresses surprise that self-nature is originally pure, undying and complete. The Fifth Patriarch recognizes this realization and entrusts robe and teaching. The selected words are Huineng's direct reply, not the Fifth Patriarch's statement.

Senses.PreferredTarget: Everywhere bright and radiant
Senses.Note: The older tree case opposes flourishing brightness to withered plainness. Jiqi refuses to make either description decisive, and Yunsou revoices both sides while saying arising and ceasing have no separate mark to grasp. Xuefeng raises his staff and opens a way for the bright side. Muan joins brightness with freedom in every place; Chushi places it on the busy street against the stillness of a solitary peak. Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J24/J24nB138.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Yunmen Kuangzhen. Yunmen raises Mazu Daoyi's saying that all language belongs to the Deva school and praises it, but complains that no one asks. The selected words are Mazu's quoted maxim; Yunmen uses it to provoke a live question rather than to define a sect.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J27/J27nB192.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Daxiu Zhu. Daxiu Zhu owns the retained deployment, ruling the porridge and rice, the walking and sitting, each stirring and stillness all not in the bowl of the world, with Bodhidharma as fellow traveler for the one who knows.

Senses.Explanation: A paired unit naming each stirring and each stillness of the day, listed beside its sibling pairs and ruled on wherever the records locate the working. Ying'an Tanhua rules that to say the thus-come one is seen in the twelve double-hours' each stirring and stillness, word and silence, turn and bow is taking the thief for a son — and to say he is not discerned there is madness running outward; Mi'an Xianjie strings the pairs on the hall seat — one advance one retreat, one stirring one stillness, trust the naga ever in composure — with one seize one release, one kill one quicken, the Jiazhou elephant salt-heavy and the Shanfu iron bull thirsty; Wuzhun Shifan, before the assembly, holds that once the shapes of stirring and stillness cannot be found, each stirring and stillness, exit and entry, release and gather, advance and retreat is nowhere other than the playground of the uncanny light and freedom; and Cishou Huaishen, taking leave of the assembly, likens it to the wild crane's wheeling and the floating clouds' gathering and scattering — no north or south, no coming or going, the wayfarer's heart just so. Tianru Weize runs his own day before the assembly — rising, washing, porridge, sweeping leaves, watching the fish, one word one silence, one stirring one stillness — hawking the assembly's life-lord without pause through the six watches of day and night; Qianyan Yuanzhang ties it to the one sentence: today's doing clear, then each stirring and stillness, word and silence, rise and fall, birth and death — living just so, dying just so; Guting Shanjian hatches his bird on it — brooding without losing the clutch through stirring and stillness until the shell falls apart and the lively one hops out knowing hunger and fullness, feathers whole, flying where it will; and Daxiu Zhu, reversing Gaofeng Yuanmiao's bowl of the world, rules the porridge and rice, the dung and water, the walking and sitting, each stirring and stillness all not in it — know that and Bodhidharma becomes one's fellow traveler; miss it and one boils tea with water and cooks rice with rice.

Senses.PreferredTarget: A teacher of fifteen hundred people, yet he does not even grasp the point of the exchange
AlternateTargets: With fifteen hundred students, he still misses what this question is about
SearchAliases: Sansheng fifteen hundred teacher misses point exchange
Xuefeng net fish fifteen hundred students Chan
Senses.Note: Sansheng asks Xuefeng what a fish that has escaped the net eats. Xuefeng says he will answer when Sansheng is out of the net; Sansheng then delivers this rebuke. Feiyin, Poshan, Wanru, Sanyi, Sanshan, and Qianyan separately comment or write verses on the exchange. Their judgments divide between Sansheng's daring challenge and Xuefeng's deflection. The exact line is Sansheng's quoted speech, not the later commentators' own accusation.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J26/J26nB178.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Feiyin. Feiyin Tongrong recounts the old exchange: Sansheng asks what a golden-scaled fish that has passed through the net eats; Xuefeng says he will answer when Sansheng gets out of the net; Sansheng rebukes the teacher of fifteen hundred monks for missing the question; Xuefeng replies that he is busy with abbey duties. Feiyin calls the two old masters' moves a push and pull and, for the present audience, offers his own imagined answer about cooking the marrow of empty space. The headword is Sansheng's rebuke inside the cited case, not Feiyin's new answer.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J26/J26nB177.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Poshan. Poshan Haiming cites the same Sansheng and Xuefeng fish-through-the-net exchange, including Sansheng's rebuke and Xuefeng's reply about abbey duties. He then comments that the two nets are not the same and adds a verse about the fish still driven by hunger and caught in waves. The headword is Sansheng's old spoken turn; Poshan's comment and verse are a later assessment of the pair's maneuver, not a fresh rebuke to a teacher of fifteen hundred monks.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J27/J27nB189.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Sanyi Yu. Sanyi Mingyu has been urging teachers to show skill in changing host and guest rather than trading stock phrases. He then cites Sansheng's question about a fish beyond the net, Xuefeng's deferred answer, Sansheng's rebuke, and Xuefeng's busy-abbot reply. Sanyi likens the two to powerful birds and says it is easier to play Xuefeng than Sansheng, who must pass through weapons without a scratch. The headword is Sansheng's old challenge; Sanyi uses it to illustrate demanding live responsiveness.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J29/J29nB244.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Sanshanlai. Sanshan Denglai quotes the old exchange in which Sansheng asks what a fish beyond the net eats, rebukes Xuefeng for missing the question, and hears Xuefeng reply that his abbey duties are heavy. Sanshan praises Sansheng's bold charge and Xuefeng's self-effacing retreat, saying both emerge unhurt, then adds his own verse and warns readers not to wrong the old teachers if they do not see the move. Qianyan Yuanzhang reproduces the Sansheng and Xuefeng exchange and follows it with a new verse picturing a golden-scaled fish rushing through waves toward Dragon Gate. ClaimAnchors.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J26/J26nB178.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Feiyin. Feiyin Tongrong recounts the old exchange: Sansheng asks what a golden-scaled fish that has passed through the net eats; Xuefeng says he will answer when Sansheng gets out of the net; Sansheng rebukes the teacher of fifteen hundred monks for missing the question; Xuefeng replies that he is busy with abbey duties. Feiyin calls the two old masters' moves a push and pull and, for the present audience, offers his own imagined answer about cooking the marrow of empty space. The headword is Sansheng's rebuke inside the cited case, not Feiyin's new answer.

ClaimAnchors.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J27/J27nB189.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Sanyi Yu. Sanyi Mingyu has been urging teachers to show skill in changing host and guest rather than trading stock phrases. He then cites Sansheng's question about a fish beyond the net, Xuefeng's deferred answer, Sansheng's rebuke, and Xuefeng's busy-abbot reply. Sanyi likens the two to powerful birds and says it is easier to play Xuefeng than Sansheng, who must pass through weapons without a scratch. ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 敬王。陛下問處便是，管取龍顏大喜。休擬議，擬議白雲萬里。洞山。僧問：「如何是佛？」山云：「麻三斤。」秤頭有紐，秤尾無星。一個錘推上推下，兩片皮說重說輕。若是牙郎主人，豈定道麻三斤。木平問洛浦：「一漚未發時如何？」浦云：「移舟諳水脈，舉棹別波瀾。」平不契，復問蟠龍，龍云：「移舟不別水，舉棹即迷源。」平大悟。雲峰悅云：「木平於洛浦言下悟去，猶較些子，可惜向蟠龍死水中淹殺。」如何活水不藏龍，情願淹他死水中。提起當年虀甕看，不堪惆悵動悲風。投子指菴前一片石，謂雪峰云：「三世諸佛總在裏許。」峰云：「還有不在裏許者麼？」子云：「不快漆桶。」不快漆桶，團圞無縫。一擔兩頭，中間最重。堪笑翁翁只賣油，勘破須還老趙州。巖頭銅沙鑼裏滿盛油。暉天露刃七星流，擬欲抬眸斬卻頭，平地死人無數數，銅沙鑼裏滿盛油。子胡看狗。見有人來便咬殺，帶牌惡犬甚猙獰。是渠佛性都無了，情愿輪迴墮畜生。三聖問雪峰：「透網金鱗，未審何以為食？」峰云：「待汝出網來向汝道。」聖云：「一千五百人善知識，話頭也不識。」峰云：「老僧住持事繁。」透網金鱗衝浪來，龍門萬仞碧崔嵬。不遭點額還燒尾，閃電光中吼怒雷。雲門示眾云：「聞聲悟道，見色明心。觀世音菩薩將錢買胡餅，放下手元來卻是饅頭。」雲門氣宇如王，偏要剜肉作瘡。觀音菩薩買胡餅，也是雪上加霜。雲門示眾云：「乾坤之內，宇宙之間，中有一寶，秘在形山。拈燈籠來佛殿裏，將山門向燈籠上。」無明有一寶，青黃赤白皁。深山開鋪席，鬧市沿門叫。賣與世間人，可憐都不要。黑漆皮燈籠，撞著呵呵笑。雲門。僧問：「如何是清淨法身？」門云：「花藥欄。」僧云：「便與麼去時如何？」門云：「金毛師子。」花藥欄，淨法身，金毛師子玉麒麟。舌頭無骨饒陽老，那個師僧眼有筋。雲門。僧問：「如何是一代時教？」門云：「對一說。」對一說，八十翁翁嚼生鐵。咬卻舌，流出血，萬象光中寒凜冽。明眼禪和總不知，剛把烏龜喚作鱉。雲門。僧問：「不是目前機，亦非目前事時如何？」門云：「倒一說。」百億山河皆帝闕，古今日月一雙眸。不知那個無思算，獨據毘盧頂上頭。雲門。僧問：「如何是法身？」門云：「六不收。」六不收，一拳拳倒黃鶴樓，題詩崔顥今何在，萬古長江空自流。翠巖參禪師夏末示眾云：「一夏已來為兄弟說話，看翠巖眉毛在麼？」保福云：「作賊人心虛。」長慶云：「生也

Senses.Explanation: Sansheng's rebuke belongs to one inherited exchange with Xuefeng about a fish through the net; six later masters reproduce and assess that same event. Feiyin Tongrong recounts the old exchange: Sansheng asks what a golden-scaled fish that has passed through the net eats; Xuefeng says he will answer when Sansheng gets out of the net; Sansheng rebukes the teacher of fifteen hundred monks for missing the question; Xuefeng replies that he is busy with abbey duties. Feiyin calls the two old masters' moves a push and pull and, for the present audience, offers his own imagined answer about cooking the marrow of empty space. The headword is Sansheng's rebuke inside the cited case, not Feiyin's new answer. Poshan Haiming cites the same Sansheng and Xuefeng fish-through-the-net exchange, including Sansheng's rebuke and Xuefeng's reply about abbey duties. He then comments that the two nets are not the same and adds a verse about the fish still driven by hunger and caught in waves. The headword is Sansheng's old spoken turn; Poshan's comment and verse are a later assessment of the pair's maneuver, not a fresh rebuke to a teacher of fifteen hundred monks. Wanru Tongwei raises the old fish-through-the-net case to the assembly. After Sansheng's rebuke that a teacher of fifteen hundred does not recognize the question and Xuefeng's answer about abbey duties, Wanru says one move is hard as iron and the other soft as cotton, with each useful in its own way. He imagines a monk objecting to this judgment and says he would give him twenty staff blows as a reward for daring. Sansheng remains the speaker of the quoted headword; Wanru is the present judge of both replies. Sanyi Mingyu has been urging teachers to show skill in changing host and guest rather than trading stock phrases. He then cites Sansheng's question about a fish beyond the net, Xuefeng's deferred answer, Sansheng's rebuke, and Xuefeng's busy-abbot reply. Sanyi likens the two to powerful birds and says it is easier to play Xuefeng than Sansheng, who must pass through weapons without a scratch. Occurrences.Kwic: 悟斯《經》者不過數十言，微塵剎海無量法門全體窺矣！如其用力微而克功遠，惟《般若波羅蜜多心經》歟！絕學居士自言一生在《般若心經》得力，及見《心經標言》，分經析義如檢自家屋裏珍奇，纖無疑滯。其辭匹鏡花水月、其義奪杲日晴空，性相全彰、宗教圓備，豈非剖一微塵見大千經卷者哉？惜未見其人，但從其子頗聞居士一二進止，其子凝之穎悟超拔可克父業。庚申秋，馳書及壙記《標言》，求予一言乃就梓。茲見居士脫體受用全在般若光中，焚香合爪讚歎，真世諦中法眼再來人也。是為序。金剛般若經四依解序《金剛般若經四依解》序原夫！如來為一大事因緣出現于世，開示悟入佛之知見，故佛知見者即阿耨多羅三藐三菩提是也。如來一代藏教唯此一事，但隨眾生心量所見不同，故有五時設化之別。初演太華嚴正示菩提自相，主伴融通，依正無礙，一即一切，一切即一，總之是無上菩提不思議境相也。當時二乘人在會如聾若啞，其凡夫可知。如來不得已將此不思議菩提分示少許，以就下劣根器。三乘人同見丈六金身，說《阿含》等教；二乘人始得信入，依之出分斷生死、證有餘涅槃，名人空般若，是少分菩提，即自覺也。以二乘根器狹劣得少為足，自任是二乘，耽涅槃、怖生死，不能進修無上菩提，故如來說方等大乘等教，彈偏斥小、贊大褒圓，激勵二乘發大乘之心，此示半分菩提亦能自他俱覺也。二乘凡夫見佛彈斥，乃愧小忻大、厭偏慕圓，雖欲發大乘心而執實有大乘小乘法相，不能發清淨菩提心，故佛復說般若空教破前

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 法身，流出無邊諸三昧海，文殊、普賢大人境界，德山、臨濟向上提持，此方、他方齊成佛道，有說、無說俱轉法輪，極三際為一時，統十方為一剎，二十四氣、七十二候、三百六十五日只在剎那，悟之則當念圓明，迷之則永沈生死。復舉：保寧永和尚示眾云：世尊不說說，迦葉不聞聞。卓拄杖，云：水流黃葉來何處？牛帶寒鴉過遠村。師云：青州棃，鄭州棗，大抵無過出處好。歲旦，上堂。半夜起來，赴省堂焚祝。焚祝了，丞相府諸衙門人事。人事畢，即回殿堂行香，撒沙呪土，遶廊行道。次第諸山報禮，准備接官。若作新年頭佛法會，入地獄如箭射。進退兩班。上堂：虎豹文章，全歸爪牙之力；鯤鵬變化，心藉羽翼之功。法社要在人，叢林自然增氣。睦州佐黃檗，楊岐輔慈明，相與建法幢，展衲僧巴鼻。元宵，上堂。一切月以一月為真，一切燈以一燈為體，一即一切，一切即一，一從什麼處起？洎合錯下註脚。諸山講主至，上堂。先聖道：諸法不自生，亦不從他生，不共不無因，是故說無生。盡大地是胡餅，任你橫咬竪咬，西天那爛陀寺裏一萬來僧人人得喫，只有摩訶迦羅大神不得喫，把須彌山一摑百襍碎，帝釋𨁝跳上梵天去也。上堂：即心即佛，禍不入慎家之門。非心非佛，舌是斬身之斧。古人的今人用，今人的古人為。一犬吠虗，千猱啀實。鳳山今日不惜性命，與你諸人抽釘󳫠楔去也。茶！佛涅槃，上堂：東西南北，空中鳥跡；南北西東，水底魚蹤。瞿曇用盡平生力，直至而今歸不得。忽都達兒狀元入山，上堂。舉：玉泉浩布褌

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: ，打人打斷脊梁、罵人罵入骨髓，惡名遍滿江湖，禿丁真箇莽鹵。有人打算飯錢，未審將何抵補？卻有箇抵補處，春山疊亂青，春水漾虛碧，寥寥天地間，獨立望何極？設有道：『者箇說話有甚麼交涉？』沒交涉，有來歷，等閒打破祖師關，逆行順行天莫測。」燈夜，小參。「萬古碧潭空界月，再三撈摝始應知，不須撈、不須摝，今年燈勝去年燈，去年月是今年月，嫂嫂的的大哥妻，上元定是元宵節。古人道我疑，千年蒼玉精，一片化為秋水骨，海神欲護護不得，一旦鼇頭忽擎出，時節因緣，端的端的。」上堂。悅眾問：「『佛法』二字即不問，如何是法慶景？」師云：「悅眾好瞌睡。」進云：「如何是景中人？」師云：「更問阿誰？」進云：「睡中作得主，其心安如海。」師云：「正鬧在。」進云：「不風流處也風流。」師云：「依舊歸堂打瞌睡。」乃云：「一即一切，一切即一，曠大劫來未曾變易，諸佛世尊是吾弟子。恁麼會，明月清風；不恁麼會，清風明月。不見昔日廣額屠兒颺下屠刀，向世尊云：『我是千佛一數。』世尊云：『如是，如是。』何似現前眾善信，遵佛教、持佛戒、發佛心、作佛事，各各遠持香華，來此萬佛道場供養百千諸佛？其為萬佛一數，決定無疑。設有問：『如何是諸佛師？』作麼生扺對？」驀拈拄杖，云：「你有拄杖子，我與你拄杖子；你無拄杖子，我奪卻你拄杖子。」擿拄杖，下座。上堂。問：「不問有言、不問無言，請師指示第一義。」師云：「庭前柏樹子圊頭。」問：「萬法歸一，一歸何處？」師云

Senses.Explanation: One is all, and all is one: the formula joins a single source or act with its many expressions. Masters use it in teaching without letting it become an empty slogan. Chushi compares one moon with its many reflections and one lamp with its many lights, then asks where the one begins. Tianan says the relation has not changed across ages; Zhuanyu uses it to explain the mutual inclusion of phenomena. Yuan applies the relation to compassionate appearances in many places. Wuming joins it to realizing mind in all phenomena, then insists that the listener investigate rather than merely recite.

Senses.Explanation: An impossible-scale condition in Mazu Daoyi's answer to Pang Yun: Pang asks, 'Who is the one who is not a companion to the myriad things?' and Mazu replies, 'When you drink up all the West River's water in one mouthful, I will tell you.' Later records preserve that condition as a named case line, quote it, turn it into a fresh question, answer it, and build new physical challenges from it. Baiyun Shouduan says that after the one-mouthful drink no drop remains through all antiquity, then calls Mazu's mouth regrettably narrow. An unnamed music-bureau officer sets the West River line aside and asks Yunding Defu to swallow the dismounting platform; Yunding spreads both hands and requests that it be brought. An unnamed monk asks Yuanwu Keqin what about drinking the river, and Yuanwu answers, 'The bright sun adorns the sky.' Wuzu Fayan repeats the line to his assembly and extends it to reaching the bottom of a ten-thousand-fathom pool. Wuchu Daguan quotes Mazu and supplies a different answer to Pang's question, waiting for empty space to fall. These are attested continuations of one Mazu line; the entry does not turn the impossible act into an unstated universal meaning.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J38/J38nB406.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Tianran of Mount Lu. Tianran Hanshi asks listeners to examine whether they can remain in charge when circumstances and old habits press them. Even if reasoning seems to settle feelings now, he asks whether that strength will still help when the next breath does not come and another life begins. Senses.Explanation: One phrase or one sentence is a counted unit of wording whose force depends on its setting, not a single universal formula. In Linji Yixuan's record, an unnamed monk asks for the first phrase (第一句), and Linji says that one phrase must contain three mysteries and that each mystery must contain three essentials. Yuanwu Keqin says that penetrating one phrase brings thousands of phrases through at once. In a New Year's address, Yulin Tongxiu announces one phrase that buddhas, patriarchs, and his own teacher had not spoken, then gives it to the assembly. Baiyan Fu's signed preface uses one word and one phrase (一字一句) for the smallest units said never ultimately to have been spoken. Elsewhere Yulin warns that one fitting phrase can tether a donkey for ten thousand ages, while Muchen Daomin asks for a phrase outside the pattern.

Senses.PreferredTarget: One phrase contains three mysteries; one mystery contains three essentials
AlternateTargets: Within one saying are three mysteries, and within one mystery are three essentials

Senses.Note: This compact Linji formula nests three mysteries in one phrase and three essentials in one mystery. Later masters use it in verse, lineage explanation, and debate about how a living response exceeds a fixed list.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J26/J26nB182.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Wanru. Wanru Tongwei opens a hall verse with the full Linji formula that one phrase holds three mysteries and each mystery three essentials. Instead of defining the numbers, he follows it with a blue sky taking a blow, the sun shining, a wooden boy riding a crane, a stone woman adorning herself, and objects that laugh or speak. He asks what they say and, after a pause, gives a line about Vipassi Buddha. The formula is Wanru's present opening to an impossible-image verse and a question to the assembly, not a numbered list of nine fixed answers.

Occurrences.Kwic: 一心之法印定，故末後拈花微笑嫡付教外單傳。至二十八代達磨東來，傳至六祖，亦無非一心之法。彼群英疊出，兩派分岐，旁出繁興，皆以所得淺深教化。馬大師單提向上，百丈再參，而末後一喝。黃檗因聞，不覺吐舌，纔明大師大機大用，故施棒以接臨濟。如發藥人，只欲救病。今來書云：「只有三頓痛棒，未聞有兩頓四頓之旨。」此語若在臨濟則可，在黃檗則不可。何故？若黃檗恁麼為人，已成實法了也。況臨濟至大愚，言下點破、悟徹根源，握萬世之綱宗，開法四賓主、四料簡、四喝，一句中具三玄，一玄中具三要，簡別邪正，殺活縱橫。自後五宗並立，門庭雖異，總之咸歸一心之法。如洞山得法雲巖，臨行囑付，因過水睹影，大悟前旨，有偈云云，可不各各師承有據，或嚴密，或痛快。又豈有實法繫累人耶？正宗流至中峰，傳法於千巖，乃云：「失卻一隻眼。」淆訛從此而起。此何說也？況中峰大師語錄，言言見諦，句句超宗，其《道要歌》發明玄要，字字破的。及餘開示、小參、拈提公案，當時無有出其右者。而千巖築破方甓，盡底掀翻，中峰尚囑云：「時節若至，其理自彰。」後三十年，住山出世
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J25/J25nB171.xml). Recorded Sayings of Monk Tianyin. In a letter answering a correspondent's question about Huangbo's blows, Tianyin Yuanxiu traces the teaching through Bodhidharma and later masters. He says Linji was brought to insight at Dayu, then opened methods of host and guest, selections, shouts, and the formula that one phrase has three mysteries and one mystery three essentials. Tianyin argues that such methods distinguish true from false without turning Huangbo's three blows into a fixed rule that must always be repeated. The headword is Tianyin's cited account of Linji's teaching in this current letter, not a fresh utterance placed in Linji's mouth inside a quoted dialogue.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J33/J33nB294.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Liangting Ting of Yunxi. Liangting Jingting criticizes later readers who cut Fenyang's verse and Shitou's writings into separate clauses to force them into three-mystery labels. In his own comparison he places the five positions beside the formula that one phrase contains three mysteries and each mystery three essentials, while warning that one cannot simply twist the five positions and three mysteries together. He allows an interpretive label when it follows the old masters' point but rejects a rigid word-by-word gloss. The headword serves his argument against mechanical classification.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J34/J34nB299.xml). Recorded Sayings of Monk Sanfeng Zang. At a hall address requested by a lay patron, Hanyue Fazang strikes the ground with his staff and traces this teaching strike through Huangbo and his own teacher Tiantong. He strikes again, says the one phrase and three mysteries formula breaks any fixed notion of a single staff blow or shout, and strikes once more while explaining that neither the earlier nor later blow can be handled as a stock technique. The headword is Hanyue's present account of flexible use in this staged action, not a literal count of strikes or a quotation spoken by Huangbo.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X82/X82n1571.xml). Complete Five Lamps, Jianzhou Chongfan Yu section: an unnamed monk asks whether Chongfan receives someone who comes this way, then someone who does not. Its modifiers specify what the answer must do: express gratitude, pass through the skull, overturn mountains, establish a household, or avoid the sacred and ordinary. Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (T/T47/T47n1999.xml). Recorded Sayings of Monk Mi’an (密菴和尚語錄): Mi'an Xianjie applies the donkey-stake verdict to polished metaphysical phrasing.

Senses.Explanation: One phrase that fits the head is not praise for a correct answer: it is the stock warning that a perfectly matching formulation can tether a donkey for ten thousand ages. Gulin Qingmao applies the verdict to an unnamed questioner's apparently sweeping response and calls him badly unawake. Yuanwu Keqin gives the same truncating reply in an interview; Xuedou Chongxian raises Yunmen's formula while asking how to escape its fault. An older record asks for a replacement that avoids the fault. Shending Hongyin asks for a nonmatching phrase, rejects the offered answer as matching exactly, and says the sinker has fallen into the well. Mi'an Xianjie applies the formula to polished metaphysical wording.

Tianan Sheng asks a monk how other places compare with here. When the monk says there is not a hair of difference, Tianan replies with the donkey-tether warning and drives him out with his staff. The line rejects the monk neat formula. Yinyuan Longqi asks his small-talk assembly how to understand the three unattainable times. Even claiming to gain what cannot be gained risks becoming a fitting phrase and long tether; denying it gives no ground. He blocks a settled answer. Xun the senior monk asks Zixian Jue about illuminating before using. Zixian answers with the donkey-tether warning, then responds to the next question about reversing that order. It is his direct reply to Xun. Feiyin Tongrong quotes Chuanzi asking Jiashan where he learned a claim beyond seeing and hearing. Chuanzi gives the exact donkey-tether warning. Feiyin repeats its danger, asks how his assembly can get free, and strikes the incense table. Chuanzi is the quoted speaker; Feiyin is the current critic.

Entries.SourceTerm: 一句子當明不當照，一句子當照不當明

Senses.PreferredTarget: One saying should make clear without illuminating; another should illuminate without making clear.
AlternateTargets: One phrase is for clarity rather than illumination, the other for illumination rather than clarity.
SearchAliases: clear not illuminate illuminate not clear
Senses.Note: Two masters quote an inherited contrast of clarity and illumination, then ask different live questions about its four modes or their coincidence.

Occurrences.Kwic: 正當霜桂花開夜，又是蟠桃結實時。入院，上堂云：危巒蕭灑古禪宮，信步重歸趣無窮。風卷白雲天界淨，一輪紅日正當空。當日，知事請小參，云：銀臺燃鳳燭，𦦨照虗堂；寶閣扣金鐘，聲騰空界。於是慧光無間，冥通先佛之妙心；雅梵喧轟，潛運祖師之密旨。識情未盡，舉目皆差；根境頓忘，殊途一致。若能如是，始解帶角披毛。雖然恁麼，大洪拄杖猶未肯在。敢問諸人：且道拄杖子別有甚麼長處？良久，云：天教生在千峰上，穩密盤根勢未休。上堂云：曉風吹散碧天雲，日上長空景象分。寂照含虗無內外，當明一句若為論？所以道：一句子當明不當照，一句子當照不當明。一句子明暗混融，一句子不落明暗。四句中且道：那一句為賓？那一句為主？若也委悉得去，便乃行脚事畢。苟或未然，萬古碧潭空界月，再三撈摝始應知。冬夜，小參。好諸禪德！金鐘雖韻，星月未分，假燈燭為光明，仗聲塵為佛事。於是，熒煌交映，音韻相和，逈出見聞，遐超聲色。所以道：欲識解脫道，諸法不相到，眼耳絕見聞，聲色閙浩浩。諸人若也於斯委悉得去，可謂如龍得水、似虎依山；苟或未然，不免他旋轉。大洪今夜不惜眉毛為諸人說破：耳界聞時眼界通，一根旋返六圓融，欲知佛祖虗明地，妙在聲香味觸中。冬節，上

Occurrences.Kwic: 機前，不勞呈巧妙。僧云：恁麼則一句靈然，通途絕朕。師云：是阿那箇一句？僧擬議，師云：過犯彌天。師乃云：剎塵一掃，大小量空；念劫兩融，前後際斷。不離當處，圓應無窮；安住是中，周施不怠。正恁麼時，木童敲月戶，六用虗明；石筍暗抽條，孤標秀密。且道是誰境界？江岸風濤急，蘆村景色幽。上堂，云：見聞不昧，聲色純真，動靜無虧，去留本妙。若也盡底承當得去，始信法法圓成，便能隨處立宗，返常合道。其或未然，滿襟秋露濕，一鑑冷無痕。上堂。云：未休休去，未歇歇去，豁然寶鏡當臺，無限清光滿戶。所以道：一句子當明不當照，一句子當照不當明。若或當照當明，又作麼生？枯枝頭上雪，不待大陽春。上堂云：莫怪石頭饒舌，便道靈源明皎潔。功成照不失虗，妙盡明無間歇。如今果爾難藏，盡逐秋光漏泄。為報海內道人，參取箇中時節。上堂，僧問：午燈非照燭，夜炬滿天紅時如何？師云：猶墮傍來路。僧云：如何是向上之機？師云：明暗盡時俱不照。師乃云：披毛遊火聚，焰裏藏身；戴角混塵泥，光中轉步。靈珠絕點，卞玉無瑕，一念廓融，千機秀發。正恁麼時，坐却傍來路子。更有道得底。歷然超化表，浩劫體難分。上堂。云：明簾未捲，祕殿舒光，妙體潛彰，真機尚密。直

Entries.SourceTerm: 一句定乾坤、一劍平天下

Senses.PreferredTarget: one phrase settles heaven and earth and one sword pacifies all under heaven
AlternateTargets: a single phrase fixes the cosmos while a single sword brings peace to the realm
Senses.Note: The lamp recension and Huqiu record are recensions of one sermon and count as one use.

Occurrences.Kwic: 盡大地既如粟米粒大，只如森羅萬象、人畜草芥，著在什麼處？師云：此問不惡。僧云：豈無方便？師云：棒打不死。僧禮拜。師云：救得一半。師乃云：寰中天子勑，塞外將軍令，一句定乾坤，一劍平天下，便見時康道泰，四海晏清。向我衲僧門下又且不然，拄杖子吞却乾坤了也，綿綿不漏絲毫，何處更有一物與諸人為緣為對？還會麼？良
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X69/X69n1358.xml). Huqiu Shaolong: Sayings (虎丘紹隆禪師語錄). Speaker: Huqiu Shaolong.
Occurrences.VariantForm: 一句定乾坤，一劍平天下

Senses.Explanation: Huqiu Shaolong pairs imperial command with military command: one phrase settles heaven and earth and one sword pacifies the realm. He then contrasts this ordered world with his patch-robed gate, where the staff swallows heaven and earth. Huqiu's own sayings record preserves the sermon; the Orthodox Lamp repeats it as the same inherited address.

Senses.PreferredTarget: one sentence fixes the guiding rule of the school
SearchAliases: a sentence fixes the main rule
Senses.Note: Four named current speakers; the line answers, caps, imagines, and tests the claim of a decisive lineage phrase.

Occurrences.Kwic: 州進云料揀已蒙師指示如今佛法囑何人師云橫身當宇宙一句定綱宗進云學人分上又作麼生師打云正好喫棒乃云不登寶位頓
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (L/L158/L158n1652.xml). In Mingjue Cong record, a monk has asked him to sort the four Linji alternatives and then asks who will inherit the Buddha teaching. Mingjue answers that a single phrase sets the lineage rule; when the monk asks what that means for him, Mingjue strikes him. The line is Mingjue answer, not the monk question.

Occurrences.Kwic: 擬議即沒交涉。大眾還會麼？拈得便用、把得便撲，一句定綱宗，青天飛雪雹。卓主丈，下座。上堂：如來非智巧，智者必以如來為宗；
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X71/X71n1412.xml). Gulin Qingmao recalls Shoushan warning that merely deciding to sit or stand misses the encounter. Addressing his own assembly, Gulin asks if they understand, says to use what is at hand, and caps the talk with the single-phrase line and snow falling from a clear sky before striking his staff. The phrase claims practical command in his present address.

Occurrences.Kwic: 肘後符靈底出來，掀倒禪床，喝散大眾，橫身當宇宙，一句定綱宗。秉拂上座有口，秪宜壁上閣。然事無一向，隨時應節
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J28/J28nB202.xml). At a winter-solstice whisk talk, Baichi Xingyuan imagines a person with the eye and skill to overturn the teaching seat and shout the assembly away. Senses.Note: The local challenge and the current teacher's response govern the reading; quoted evaluations are not universal factual claims. The variant 一句當天，八萬生死門永絕 moves birth-and-death into the noun phrase for the gates, whereas the canonical wording says the gates end birth-and-death. Both literal readings are preserved.

Occurrences.Kwic: 夫佛出世者，元無出入。名相無體，道本如如。法爾天真，不同修證。只要虗閑不昧，作用不涉塵泥。箇中纖毫道不盡，即為魔王眷屬。句前句後，是學人難處。所以一句當天，八萬門永絕生死。直饒得似秋潭月影，靜夜鐘聲，隨扣擊以無虧，觸波瀾而不散，猶是生死岸頭事。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X67/X67n1309.xml). Treasury of the True Dharma Eye. Xuansha Shibei's 'One sentence fills the sky; the myriad gates end birth and death' occurs in a discourse preserved in Dahui's collection. He first says that names and forms lack a fixed substance and the way is naturally thus, rather than something manufactured through attainment. Yet leaving even a hair's breadth unexpressed makes one a follower of the demon king; what comes before and after the sentence is the learner's difficulty. The sweeping declaration is immediately limited: even responsiveness as clear as a moon reflected in an autumn pool or a bell in the still night is still business on the shore of birth and death. The sentence cannot simply certify an attractive state of clarity as final release.

Senses.Explanation: Xuansha Shibei's 'One sentence fills the sky; the myriad gates end birth and death' occurs in a discourse preserved in Dahui's collection. The word-order form moves birth-and-death inside the noun phrase for the gates; four separate recorded uses are included. He first says that names and forms lack a fixed substance and the way is naturally thus, rather than something manufactured through attainment. Yet leaving even a hair's breadth unexpressed makes one a follower of the demon king; what comes before and after the sentence is the learner's difficulty. The sweeping declaration is immediately limited: even responsiveness as clear as a moon reflected in an autumn pool or a bell in the still night is still business on the shore of birth and death. The sentence cannot simply certify an attractive state of clarity as final release. Wuyi Yuanlai explicitly quotes Xuansha's declaration and comments that its value lies in 'one sentence.' He expands its all-pervading reach: throughout the worlds there is no gap, image or trace, and neither Buddhas, ancestors nor living beings have a place to be installed. But he ends by asking who it is that speaks the two words 'birth and death.' The apparently comprehensive affirmation turns back upon the speaker; the quotation is a test of the source of such language, not just a numerical claim about many doors. Hanyue Fazang voices the pair in his own explanation of teaching language. The forms of sentences differ, he says, while their use is not of two kinds. He then distinguishes Linji's three sentences, spoken in terms of the learner's understanding, from Yunmen's three, spoken in terms of the teacher's application, and cites the saying that intention is not in the sentence, yet is within it. The headword thus asserts the reach of a sentence through its functioning in a teaching relation, without making every wording interchangeable or its surface meaning sufficient. Shanyi Ruchun warns against understandings that lean on grass and cling to trees. He demands that the skull be shattered and habitual nests overturned, forbidding reliance on old tracks, before calling for the one sentence and the myriad gates. Only then does he speak of showing it in every particular and responding to circumstances with unrestricted change. The violent images attack entrenched patterns of understanding; the phrase calls for living application in things and encounters, not the memorization of a single universally sufficient slogan. At a memorial for patron Yang, Jiqi Hongchu recounts an older exchange between Yang and Tangming Song. He voices the reordered one-sentence formula as his present appraisal of Yang's grasp, then warns that otherwise one must begin again. In this wording the birth-and-death gates themselves cease. In a recalled exchange, Jiqi Hongchu, called Lingyan Chu here, asks Lingshuyuan which one sentence makes the myriad birth-and-death gates cease. Lingshuyuan answers that wind passes and treetops move; his teacher tests him with further sayings. Earlier in this record the same Lingyan elder is explicitly called Lingyan Chu. Jiqi is the exact quoted questioner. Yi'an Shanzan asks a monk what the one sentence is that makes the birth-and-death gates cease. Several proposed replies follow; he challenges the last monk, strikes him when he hesitates, then answers the returned question with a shout. The line opens a current test. Eryin replies that an understanding friend is rare, then rebukes the monk's further verse, strikes him, hears his shout and strikes again. The selected words are the monk's present proposal, not Eryin's answer. In Buhui Fatong's own small-session section a monk directly offers the selected couplet. Buhui answers that an understanding friend is rare. When the monk asks if the master is seeing spots, Buhui tells him to know shame; the monk bows in a woman's manner and Buhui says he has revealed too much. The shared first responses resemble Eryin's encounter, but this record frames a present question to Buhui and continues with a distinct test; the monk speaks the couplet.

Occurrences.Kwic: 虎溪截斷鴈門關，一句臨機下口難。夜半扶桑日頭出，金雞飛上玉闌干。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X70/X70n1393.xml). Recorded Sayings of Pingshi Rudi, verse for Donglin's attendant Ren, identified in the heading as Japanese: Pingshi places the difficulty of uttering one line at the encounter between an obstructed pass and the startling scene of the sun rising at midnight. The line forms the second line of an addressed verse. This witness has no recorded questioner or failed answer, so it supports the phrase's verse use without supplying a separate encounter.

Senses.Explanation: The line contrasts stored learning with speech at the moment an encounter demands it: even one sentence can be hard to utter when the occasion is directly at hand. Baiyu Jingsi quotes it after saying that questions and answers must meet and remain connected rather than merely pour out fluently. Linquan Conglun applies it to Deshan's silence before the cake seller's question, and Shixi Xinyue uses it when a lecturer cannot answer without deliberation. Pingshi Rudi then places it in a verse for an attendant. The records make 臨機 an encountered occasion, not a request for polished recitation. Senses.Explanation: A single shout is classified through Linji’s four comparisons and through the caution that one shout may not function as a shout; its force is therefore context-dependent rather than merely numerical. Senses.Explanation: “One shout does not function as a shout” is the fourth member of Linji Yixuan’s four-shout formula, alongside the jeweled sword, crouched lion, and probing pole. Tianyin Yuanxiu explicitly quotes Linji’s set and then asks which of the four describes the shout he has just given. The retained lamp case also puts the phrase in a question answered by a rebuke. The line names one member of an inherited formula; Tianyin’s question is a present use of it.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J26/J26nB186.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Linyexi. Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J27/J27nB193.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Yinyuan. Yinyuan Longqi puts the full line to the layman Junchu and asks him to separate guest and host. Junchu shouts; Yinyuan strikes him and says he has only one fragment. Senses.Explanation: One shout distinguishes guest and host while illumination and use proceed together; these four contexts test or explain that paired claim. Linye Tongqi asks a monk to show how one shout separates guest and host while illumination and action proceed together. The monk shouts; Linye strikes him. The monk shouts again; Linye strikes him again. The line is Linye's present challenge in a sequence of tests, and the paired shouts and blows are its immediate trial; the source does not supply a tidy verbal verdict saying which participant was guest or host. Yinyuan Longqi puts the full line to the layman Junchu and asks him to separate guest and host. Junchu shouts; Yinyuan strikes him and says he has only one fragment. When Junchu hesitates, Yinyuan drives him out with more blows. AlternateTargets: A shout separates host and guest, while revealing and acting happen in the same moment

Senses.Note: The first clause says one shout distinguishes guest and host; the second says illumination and function proceed together. Qianyan, Yun'e, Binya, Jie'an, Zixian, and Meixi voice the full pair in separate sermons, often accompanying it with a shout, staff, or seat strike. Their subsequent questions ask the assembly to locate guest, host, illumination, and function in the present action. A shorter public headword has only the guest-host half; the full pair is needed for the illumination-and-function test.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J32/J32nB273.xml). Recorded Sayings of Monk Qianyan. Qianyan Yuanzhang tells the assembly that one shout distinguishes guest and host and brings illumination and use together. He shouts, asks which of those four terms applies, shouts again and momentarily says this is each of them, then shouts again and denies all four labels before asking what it is. He closes by warning against stepping forward for an explanation. The repeated shouts make the paired line a live test of fixed classifications, not a simple one-to-one chart of roles.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J28/J28nB204.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Binya. After replying to questions from monks about the hall and entry into the Way, Binya Jian strikes the Chan seat and voices the paired line. He follows it with images of white waves on a mountain and red dust beneath the sea and says one who understands it can make noon strike the third watch. He then sets aside understanding and cites an old question about what happens to the vine when the tree falls. The headword is Binya's present pivot from question-and-answer to a verse and further test.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J29/J29nB233.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Jie’an Jin. At a sermon marking his emergence as abbot and the completion of a Buddha hall, Jie'an Jin speaks of the assembled community's work and asks whether there is still an upward matter. After a pause he shouts and ends with the line that one shout separates guest and host while illumination and use happen together. The phrase is the close of his current institutional occasion and challenge, not a reply by the earlier monks in the sermon or by the next birthday-sermon participants.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J33/J33nB287.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Zixianjue. In a short hall address Zixian Jue first states that one shout distinguishes guest and host while illumination and use proceed together. He then gives a shout and asks the assembly whether it is guest or host; those who can separate them have an opening, while others still have work ahead. The headword is Zixian's own immediate challenge, and the source supplies no recorded successful answer from the assembly.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J39/J39nB447.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Meixi Du of Dongshan. On arriving at Yuantong Temple, Meixi Fudu opens his first hall sermon by saying he must make the teaching accessible to those present. He gives a forceful shout and asks whether they heard it, saying that hearing here makes the paired claim about guest, host, illumination and use clear. He shouts again and asks which role and function this shout has, urging those who cannot see it yet to examine the matter at Yuantong. The phrase is Meixi's present test in a new abbacy, not an old quotation assigned to Linji.

ClaimAnchors.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J32/J32nB273.xml). Recorded Sayings of Monk Qianyan. Qianyan Yuanzhang tells the assembly that one shout distinguishes guest and host and brings illumination and use together. He shouts, asks which of those four terms applies, shouts again and momentarily says this is each of them, then shouts again and denies all four labels before asking what it is. He closes by warning against stepping forward for an explanation. The repeated shouts make the paired line a live test of fixed classifications, not a simple one-to-one chart of roles.

When a visiting monk arrives, Yun'e Xi raises and strikes his staff and gives a shout before voicing the paired line. He says the shout splits the peach pit and reveals the person within, then asks what further explanation is needed once that person is seen. His following images insist that guest remains guest and host remains host, yet asks how their fit can be spoken. The headword belongs to Yun'e's present welcoming sermon and its staff-and-shout action, not the visitor's speech.

ClaimAnchors.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J28/J28nB204.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Binya. After replying to questions from monks about the hall and entry into the Way, Binya Jian strikes the Chan seat and voices the paired line. He follows it with images of white waves on a mountain and red dust beneath the sea and says one who understands it can make noon strike the third watch. He then sets aside understanding and cites an old question about what happens to the vine when the tree falls. The headword is Binya's present pivot from question-and-answer to a verse and further test.

ClaimAnchors.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J29/J29nB233.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Jie’an Jin. At a sermon marking his emergence as abbot and the completion of a Buddha hall, Jie'an Jin speaks of the assembled community's work and asks whether there is still an upward matter. After a pause he shouts and ends with the line that one shout separates guest and host while illumination and use happen together. The phrase is the close of his current institutional occasion and challenge, not a reply by the earlier monks in the sermon or by the next birthday-sermon participants.

ClaimAnchors.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J33/J33nB287.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Zixianjue. In a short hall address Zixian Jue first states that one shout distinguishes guest and host while illumination and use proceed together. He then gives a shout and asks the assembly whether it is guest or host; those who can separate them have an opening, while others still have work ahead.
